figures.caption: Figure 1: Multimodal EEG landscape and representative results. (a) Physiological information captured by common companion signals. (b) Publication trends, task-wise multimodal prevalence, and companion modality availability, based on prior surveys (Lee et al., 2025; Yeung & Chu, 2022). (c) Balanced accuracy on six held-out target datasets, comparing three EFM backbones with and without ZeroMAG against SleepFM and PhysioOmni.

Figure 2: Overview of ZeroMAG. The framework combines a configuration-invariant multimodal adapter, target-derived condition construction, and function-constrained conditional generation for zero-shot adapter synthesis.

Table 1: Balanced accuracy (%, mean±std over five seeds) on six held-out target datasets. Within each EEG-backbone group, ZeroMAG and the label-free baselines use the same frozen encoder and prediction head, without target labels or target-side optimization. Supervised multimodal fine-tuning is a separate reference using target training labels and all available modalities. Bold entries indicate the best target-label-free result in each group.

Table 2: Ablation results with CBraMod, averaged over all nine held-out datasets (% B-ACC, mean±std over five seeds). Ablated results are shaded blue, and ∆ denotes the decrease from Full ZeroMAG in the same run. Ablations use a separate run under the same protocol, so Full differs from the Table 1 average.
Table A.2: Latent, condition, and optimization notation.
Table C.1: B-ACC (%, mean±std over five seeds) on CAP, DREAMER, and BCI-IV. Protocol and layout as in main Table 1.
Table C.3: Sleep staging: balanced accuracy (%, mean ± reported SD over five seeds). Bold identifies ZeroMAG in each backbone group.
Table C.4: Emotion, cognitive load, and gait: balanced accuracy (%, mean ± reported SD over five seeds). Bold identifies ZeroMAG in each backbone group.

Figure C.1: Gains in balanced accuracy over EEG-only and Direct MLP, in percentage points. Both panels use the same scale. Values are differences of means from main Table 1; no paired uncertainty or significance is inferred.
Table C.5: Arithmetic derived from main Table 1; no additional experimental runs. Recovery is 100(z − e)/(s− e) for each row.

Figure D.1: Training and deployment within one separately trained backbone instantiation. Stage 1 produces the encoder and decoder. Stage 2 uses a fixed canonical latent and propagates auxiliaryloss gradients through the frozen decoder. Deployment uses unlabeled calibration data and fixed model parameters.

Figure C.2: Means and reported±1 SD for four methods within each target. Marker shapes identify backbones. Horizontal limits vary by target to show within-target differences; all values are balanced accuracy (%).

Figure I.1: Reported generalization and source-bank summaries from the main text. Left: recovery of supervised gain for unseen combinations and held-out modality types. Right: retention of the full-bank multimodal gain when using half the source bank. The panels have different reference denominators; no seed-level intervals are inferred.
